Quick technical notes to supplement Marcus' scope — drafting the short spec now: 

- Ephemeral wrapping model: each inference session gets a short-lived session key (SSK) derived from a per-tenant KEK (Key Encryption Key) stored in the HSM. The SSK is used to wrap the data encryption key (DEK) produced per object/request. SSK TTL = 10 minutes (configurable).
- KEK options: 
  * Redwood-managed KEK in FIPS-validated HSM (default)
  * Customer BYOK: customer uploads a wrapped KEK to our HSM via remote attestation and a sealed-wrap API (customer holds the unwrapped key offline).
  * Hybrid: KEK split (threshold) between Redwood and escrow custodian for emergency unseal.
- Attestation: use TPM/HSM attestation with per-deployment nonce exchange to prove code running in the enclave signs the KEK import operation.
- Rotation: KEK rotation every 90 days recommended for enterprise; DEKs rotated per object lifecycle. Support rolling KEK swap with dual-K encryption window (configurable to 24h).
- Recovery: escrow uses a PKI-backed, time-locked transfer. For air-gapped DCs, escrow key shards are supplied on FIPS-compliant hardware tokens with out-of-band verification.

Notes / asks for EdgeHealth: 
- Confirm SSK TTL tolerance for your workloads (10m default) and any offline window requirements.
- Do you need split custody thresholds (e.g., 2-of-3) vs 1-of-1 escrow?

Attachment: ephemeral-protocol-spec.md (draft)

-Rishi

Network & deployment constraints to note for the soak tests and production: 

- Crossconnect: For BYOK and attestation flows we recommend a private crossconnect (VPC peering + static routes) or AWS PrivateLink equivalent — avoid public egress for KEK import/unwrap.
- Ports / protocols: TLS 1.3 only to the HSM gateway, mTLS for operator APIs, outbound to Redwood attestation endpoints over 443.
- Egress locking: allowlist IP ranges for Redwood control plane (we will provide per-region CIDRs).
- NAT & scaling: ephemeral wrapping will generate short-lived sessions; ensure NAT session timeouts >= SSK TTL + 30s.
- Pod identity: prefer platform-managed identities (IAM role for service account) vs static secrets for KMS clients.

Attachment: networking-ports.csv

-Soojin
Infra Security Lead | Redwood Inference

Jasper — thanks, good questions. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

- Third-party custodian: yes, we support split-KEK with an approved list of custodians (we will share SOC2 docs & candidate list). We also support 2-of-3 threshold via Shamir split with custodians as holders.
- Tamper-evident tokens: supported for air-gapped recovery; we use FIPS-validated hardware tokens and offer a notarized chain-of-custody option (requires lead time).
- Audit exports: yes — nightly push to customer S3 with signed manifest (ED25519) and gzip compression. We will provide the signing public key and verification instructions.

Proposed timeline: 
- Week 0: finalize SOW and escrow/custodian selection (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/tx/ABC123)
- Week 1: staging prep + control-plane allowlist & attestation exchange
- Week 2: run soak tests (3 scenarios) in staging and capture audit logs
